fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure; Garden Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway access point clearly so responders arriving under low-visibility conditions can locate the entry without delay.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges to maintain a clear path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the main residence to create a clear gap between plant material and the structure.
• Thin dense vegetation between the front access point and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings without obstruction.
• Keep a clear walking path between the main residence and the detached structure free of overgrown plants and debris.
• Install a gate or opening in the perimeter fencing to provide a secondary access point to the rear of the property.
• If a rear gate exists, keep it unlocked or secured with a combination lock and provide the code to your local fire department.
• Mark any gate locations on the perimeter fencing with reflective tape or signage so responders can locate them quickly at night.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of stored items that would block a fire apparatus from staging close to the residence.
• Trim shrubs and trees in landscaped areas that directly border the structure walls so responders can move around the building perimeter without obstruction.

wildfire.conditions: Large Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Near Structure; Tree Cluster; Open Green Space; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Ground Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from the large trees that hang directly over or touch the house and any outbuildings.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest the structure to create open space between individual trees and between the trees and the building.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure's walls and foundation.
• Clear ground-level vegetation growing beneath the scattered trees closest to the structure to reduce the connection between low plants and tree canopies.
• Cut back or remove shrubs that are grouped close together near any structure on the property.
• Keep the open green space areas mowed short to reduce the amount of dry ground cover that can carry fire toward the house.
• Maintain the existing separation between vegetation and structures by keeping plants from growing back into cleared areas around the building perimeter.
